Art on Tezos Friday Recap 🔔

→ @ParisPhotoFair Digital Section features @ArtverseParis with a group show curated by @bygrida on @objktone: works by @emikusano, @GrantYun2, @Reuben_Wu, @niceaunties, @g_enesiskai, @shavonnewong_. 📸

→ @artontezos_ wrapped its inaugural Berlin edition - exhibitors, collectors, communities, and partners transforming the city for an unforgettable week 🤍 Check out the recap by @nowmedia  🇩🇪

→ Art on Tezos: Buenos Aires was announced: a one-day satellite event hosted @NewtroArts during Devconnect, Nov 22. ☀️

→ The @MovingImageNYC × Tezos FA2 Fellowship held its first session - open to all, diving into FA2 contracts, blockchain as creative material, and microgrants. More sessions ahead. 📚

→ Art on Tezos Photography Prize popup this evening at ArtVerse in Paris will showcase 15 photography winners. 📷

→ Collector of the Week #22: @Vierhundertneun, a collector whose practice blends touch, intuition, and digital tactility. 👐

→ @_thisisaraid community raided the "doomscrolling >>>" curation by @kikanicolela x objktone - join the community push. ⚡️

→ New column "Seen" by @fabriziobrarez highlighting Tezos artists, first feature on @DDO__xyz. 🌟

→ @carolinesaidso announced #monotez, a black-and-white community event running Dec 2–9 🖤🤍

→ @TezosCommons hosts Artz Friday with @nejoout, painter, digital artist, and Seed Phrase artlete at @TezTones. 🎨 Hosted by @YinYangYoeshi & @Crypt0nio

→ 'Fire Flowers' @annaluciacodes debut on @editart_xyz sells out in first hours 🌼

→ objkt mag features by @ForgetDali: @sashastiles – Binary and Beyond - a deep dive into hybrid authorship, Technelegy, and post-human poetry & @larswander on computation, perception, entropy, and how systems shape the act of seeing. 💡🔤

Don't Miss:

→ @editart_xyz's gp40–gp42 this week: ‘Perception’ by @VicDoval, ‘Contiumm’ by @Reptile_tez and ‘WordHunt’ by @node1618

→ Experiments and Side Notes: Vol. 1 by @loved_orleer - a vault of unseen process work now minted📓

→FRINGE Group Drop by Creator Hub Asia - 32 newly onboarded artists incl. Pop-up event today in Ulat Kambal, Philippines. 🫶🏾

→ "Candid: Reflections After a Treatment" by @akajesstucker, a fragmented self-portrait shaped by deepfake porn datasets and AI models of her own face. Curated by @_second_guess. 👁️

→ 𝐷𝑖𝑟𝑒𝑐𝑡𝑟𝑖𝑥 by @golan - a landmark 1998 generative system released publicly for the first time 🌀

→ @Salawaki_3000’s Make Your Own Tezpole cut-outs from Art on Tezos Berlin on @TeiaCommunity - all proceeds go to the Teia fountain. ✂️

→ Soft Error. A Metamorphosis Chapter - auctions via @accomparts and curated by @VonDoyl & @YNKAdigital

→ New Session by @bootloader_art × GenArtClub - a live generative experiment exploring algorithmic authorship, process and iteration. 🧩

→ Proof of Presence by @objktlabs, bringing together the first residency cohort for their debut exhibition. Curated by @postanika.

Image: Consume by Grant Yun, collected by @sendrock

AOT Delegation Visits Nong Ya Kaew to Examine Facts, Stops to Encourage Villagers

​14 Nov. 2025

The Thai side of the ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) visited Ban Nong Ya Kaew to examine the facts, preparing to report back to Malaysia. They stopped to encourage the villagers, saying that fellow ASEAN citizens would help look after them and urging them to be strong. Villagers, in turn, requested frequent visits and commented that Cambodia is good at “creating drama.”

​The ASEAN Observer Team (AOT), led by Brigadier General Samsul Rizal Musa, the Malaysian Defence Attaché, along with representatives from Indonesia and the Philippines, visited Ban Nong Ya Kaew, Khok Sung District, Sa Kaeo Province, to investigate the facts regarding the clash that occurred on the evening of November 12.

​Colonel Chainarong Kasee, Commander of the Aranyaprathet Task Force, led the AOT team to the Thai bunker that had been fired upon by the Cambodian side. They inspected it with the forensic team to examine the bullet marks from the Cambodian firing, including the trajectory. The first point was the line of trees, which showed traces of bullets grazing the trees before penetrating the bunker behind it.

​Inside the bunker in the Ban Nong Ya Kaew area, clear bullet marks from the Cambodian side were visible. Forensic officers collected evidence around the scene, using laser equipment to demonstrate the bullet trajectories.

​Brigadier General Samsul inquired about the details of the Cambodian soldiers' position. Colonel Chainarong explained that the Cambodian soldiers were at the line of trees opposite, establishing the direction of the bullet trajectory. He noted that there are no houses in that area, so the news reported by the Cambodian side that the Thai side fired at civilians is untrue.

​The officials then brought out a projectile remaining in the bunker, which the Malaysian Defence Attaché showed to the Thai media for photographic evidence.

​Brigadier General Samsul revealed that he would take the information received today to report to the Malaysian authorities regarding the facts the Thai AOT team had gathered during the site visit. The bullet marks found were in two parts: 8 marks on the trees and 2 marks on the bunker itself. The committee has seen the actual bullet marks and the real impact in the area.

​He noted that the bullets were new but declined to specify the type of ammunition or the range and trajectory, stating that all detailed information must await the completion of the work by the Thai forensic officers before the entire incident can be confirmed.

​When asked whether the bullet trajectory from the Cambodian side into the Thai side was intended to kill the Thai officers, Brigadier General Samsul declined to comment on the issue.

​At the next stop, the AOT team visited the community hall of Ban Nong Ya Kaew to discuss the impact on the villagers. Mrs. Somporn Phetchit, the village head of Nong Ya Kaew, and representatives of the villagers communicated with the AOT team.

​Village Head Somporn recounted the incident on November 12 at 4:00 PM to Brigadier General Samsul, stating that they heard small arms fire for about 10 minutes, prompting her to announce for villagers to gather at the Village Defense Volunteer (Chor Bor Bor) post. They then heard a loud sound resembling an explosion, leading her to urge the villagers to take shelter in a safe area.

​She confirmed that the explosion-like sound came from the Cambodian side but could not specify the direction, though it was near checkpoint 34-35. 40-50 villagers evacuated to the safe zone. No one was injured, but everyone was frightened, leading them to stay at the safe location for about one night before returning to their homes.

​Subsequently, a villager rep, Aunt Waraporn from Ban Nong Ya Kaew, asked to communicate with Samsul, requesting that the committee visit the area frequently.
More: https://t.co/jX0TNRYfKZ 

​#ThailandChina #Malaysia #AOT
